title: Degree adverbs (B1)
note: Two jobs: 0–100 scale (a bit / quite / very / really / extremely) and need (too / enough / far too). Czech ne moc = not very. Not so/such, not extreme adjectives. Bank 12 = one pass. Seeded from Martina's `not so much relaxing` 2026-08-16. Rebuilt 2026-08-28 after smoke: unit had been a coursebook lump. THICKENED 2026-09-04 by the B1 agent loop: 12 -> 27 items. The 12 were one pass over the scale with one item per word; the scale words now get three or four each, the too/enough pair gets six, and both take an adverb as well as an adjective (extremely well, quite slowly, well enough). C17 - the Remember recap card is cut. Intro merged 9 cards -> 6 (a bit + quite on one card, very + really + extremely on one), because cards 1-4 each restated one row of card 0's table. C4 - the Common errors bullet bolded `not so much`, which reads as a model sentence; it is a strike now (C32). A4 - the six article demands carry the Czech demonstrative that licenses `the` (Ta voda, To pocasi, Ten vylet, To more, Ty listky) or lost the article (after a long walk). F4/F3 - `It's` and `She's` are read by the lint as possessives of unknown names; the uncontracted form is in `en` and the contraction stays in `accepts`.

cards.title: What they are
points: They name how strong an adjective is, from 0 to 100
They sit before it: **a bit** tired, **very** tired

cards.title: a bit / quite
points: **a bit** = low on the scale. **a little** sits at the same height.
**quite** is the middle — stronger than a bit, weaker than very.

cards.title: very / really / extremely
points: **very** and **really** are the same height: high.
**extremely** is the top. Nothing sits above it.

cards.title: too
points: **too** is not a 0–100 tick — it is past the need
**very** cold describes · **too** cold to swim means swimming is off

cards.title: enough
points: **enough** comes AFTER the adjective, not before

cards.title: Common errors
points: Never ~~not so much~~ in front of an adjective.

items.en: It is a bit cold.
items.cz: Je trochu zima.
accepts: It is a bit cold.
It's a bit cold.
It is a little cold.
It's a little cold.
items.explanation: a bit = low on the scale.
items.explanation_cz: a bit = nízko na stupnici.

items.en: We were quite tired after a long walk.
items.cz: Byli jsme po dlouhé procházce docela unavení.
items.gap: We were ____ tired after a long walk. (middle)
accepts: We were quite tired after a long walk.
items.explanation: quite = middle of the scale.
items.explanation_cz: quite = uprostřed stupnice.

items.en: The exam was very hard.
items.cz: Ta zkouška byla velmi těžká.
accepts: The exam was very hard.
The exam was really hard.
items.explanation: very = high on the scale. really sits here too.
items.explanation_cz: very = vysoko na stupnici. really sem patří taky.

items.en: The water is warm enough to swim in.
items.cz: Ta voda je dost teplá na koupání.
items.gap: The water is warm ____ to swim in.
accepts: The water is warm enough to swim in.
The water is warm enough to swim.
items.wrong: The water is enough warm to swim in.
items.explanation: enough after the adjective, then to: warm enough to swim in.
items.explanation_cz: enough za přídavným jménem, pak to: warm enough to swim in.

items.en: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.cz: To počasí bylo na řízení extrémně náročné.
items.gap: The weather was ____ difficult for driving. (top)
accepts: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.explanation: extremely = the top of the 0–100 scale.
items.explanation_cz: extremely = vrchol stupnice 0–100.

items.en: The trip was not very relaxing.
items.cz: Ten výlet nebyl moc odpočinkový.
accepts: The trip was not very relaxing.
The trip was not really relaxing.
items.wrong: The trip was not so much relaxing.
items.explanation: Czech *ne moc* = not very. Never *not so much relaxing*.
items.explanation_cz: České *ne moc* = not very. Nikdy *not so much relaxing*.

items.en: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.cz: To moře bylo příliš studené na koupání.
items.gap: The sea was ____ cold to swim in.
accepts: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.wrong: The sea was very cold to swim in.
items.explanation: too = past the need. *very cold* only describes.
items.explanation_cz: too = za potřebou. *very cold* jen popisuje.

items.en: He drove too fast to stop.
items.cz: Jel příliš rychle na to, aby zastavil.
accepts: He drove too fast to stop.
items.wrong: He drove very fast to stop.
items.explanation: too + adverb + to: too fast to stop.
items.explanation_cz: too + příslovce + to: too fast to stop.

items.en: Our room was not big enough for four people.
items.cz: Náš pokoj nebyl dost velký pro čtyři lidi.
items.gap: Our room was not big ____ for four people.
accepts: Our room was not big enough for four people.
Our room was not big enough for 4 people.
items.wrong: Our room was not enough big for four people.
items.explanation: enough comes AFTER the adjective: big enough.
items.explanation_cz: enough stojí AŽ ZA přídavným jménem: big enough.

items.en: She is old enough to drive.
items.cz: Je dost stará na to, aby řídila.
accepts: She is old enough to drive.
She's old enough to drive.
items.wrong: She is enough old to drive.
items.explanation: enough after the adjective, then to: old enough to drive.
items.explanation_cz: enough za přídavným jménem, pak to: old enough to drive.

items.en: The tickets were far too expensive.
items.cz: Ty lístky byly až příliš drahé.
accepts: The tickets were far too expensive.
The tickets were way too expensive.
The tickets were too expensive.
items.wrong: The tickets were very too expensive.
items.explanation: To strengthen too, use far/way. *very too* is impossible.
items.explanation_cz: Pro zesílení too: far/way. *very too* nejde.

items.en: We arrived a bit late.
items.cz: Přijeli jsme trochu pozdě.
accepts: We arrived a bit late.
We arrived a little late.
items.explanation: a bit = low on the scale, with adverbs too.
items.explanation_cz: a bit = nízko na stupnici, i u příslovcí.

items.en: The film was quite long.
items.cz: Ten film byl docela dlouhý.
accepts: The film was quite long.
items.explanation: Czech *docela* is the middle tick: **quite** long, not *very* and not *a bit*.
items.explanation_cz: České *docela* je prostřední dílek: **quite** long, ne *very* a ne *a bit*.

items.en: Honza was extremely tired after work.
items.cz: Honza byl po práci extrémně unavený.
accepts: Honza was extremely tired after work.
items.explanation: **extremely** is the top of the scale — above *very*, which is only high.
items.explanation_cz: **extremely** je vrchol stupnice — nad *very*, které je jen vysoko.

items.en: This flat is a bit small for us.
items.cz: Tenhle byt je pro nás trochu malý.
items.gap: This flat is ____ small for us. (low)
accepts: This flat is a bit small for us.
This flat is a little small for us.
items.explanation: *trochu* is the bottom of the scale: **a bit** small. *a little* is the same height.
items.explanation_cz: *trochu* je spodek stupnice: **a bit** small. *a little* je stejně vysoko.

items.en: The meeting was really useful.
items.cz: Ta porada byla opravdu užitečná.
accepts: The meeting was really useful.
The meeting was very useful.
items.explanation: **really** and **very** are the same height, so either is right here.
items.explanation_cz: **really** a **very** jsou stejně vysoko, takže tady je správně obojí.

items.en: The coffee was quite strong.
items.cz: Ta káva byla docela silná.
accepts: The coffee was quite strong.
items.explanation: **quite** strong sits between *a bit* strong and *very* strong.
items.explanation_cz: **quite** strong je mezi *a bit* strong a *very* strong.

items.en: Klara speaks English extremely well.
items.cz: Klára mluví anglicky extrémně dobře.
accepts: Klara speaks English extremely well.
items.explanation: These words work in front of an adverb too: **extremely** well.
items.explanation_cz: Tahle slova fungují i před příslovcem: **extremely** well.

items.en: We walked quite slowly.
items.cz: Šli jsme docela pomalu.
accepts: We walked quite slowly.
items.explanation: **quite** in front of an adverb: quite slowly, quite late, quite well.
items.explanation_cz: **quite** před příslovcem: quite slowly, quite late, quite well.

items.en: The hotel was not very clean.
items.cz: Ten hotel nebyl moc čistý.
accepts: The hotel was not very clean.
The hotel was not really clean.
items.wrong: The hotel was not so much clean.
items.explanation: Czech *ne moc* is **not very**. *Not so much* in front of an adjective is not English.
items.explanation_cz: České *ne moc* je **not very**. *Not so much* před přídavným jménem není angličtina.

items.en: The book was not very interesting.
items.cz: Ta kniha nebyla moc zajímavá.
accepts: The book was not very interesting.
The book was not really interesting.
items.wrong: The book was not so much interesting.
items.explanation: *ne moc zajímavá* is **not very** interesting — the same trap as *not so much*.
items.explanation_cz: *ne moc zajímavá* je **not very** interesting — stejná past jako *not so much*.

items.en: The box was too heavy to lift.
items.cz: Ta krabice byla příliš těžká na zvednutí.
items.gap: The box was ____ heavy to lift.
accepts: The box was too heavy to lift.
items.wrong: The box was very heavy to lift.
items.explanation: **too** heavy to lift means it did not get lifted. *Very heavy* would only describe it.
items.explanation_cz: **too** heavy to lift znamená, že se nezvedla. *Very heavy* by ji jen popsalo.

items.en: It was too late to call her.
items.cz: Bylo příliš pozdě na to jí volat.
items.gap: It was ____ late to call her.
accepts: It was too late to call her.
items.wrong: It was very late to call her.
items.explanation: **too** late to call = the call did not happen. That is the *to* that follows **too**.
items.explanation_cz: **too** late to call = k hovoru nedošlo. To je to *to*, které jde po **too**.

items.en: This coat is too small for me.
items.cz: Tenhle kabát je na mě příliš malý.
items.gap: This coat is ____ small for me.
accepts: This coat is too small for me.
items.wrong: This coat is very small for me.
items.explanation: **too** small for me — past what I need. *Very small* would just be a size.
items.explanation_cz: **too** small for me — za tím, co potřebuju. *Very small* by byla jen velikost.

items.en: Is your coffee hot enough?
items.cz: Je tvoje káva dost horká?
accepts: Is your coffee hot enough?
items.explanation: **enough** goes after the adjective, in a question as well: hot **enough**.
items.explanation_cz: **enough** jde za přídavné jméno, i v otázce: hot **enough**.

items.en: Eva doesn't speak English well enough.
items.cz: Eva nemluví dost dobře anglicky.
accepts: Eva doesn't speak English well enough.
Eva does not speak English well enough.
items.wrong: Eva doesn't speak English enough well.
items.explanation: **enough** follows an adverb the same way it follows an adjective: well **enough**.
items.explanation_cz: **enough** jde za příslovce stejně jako za přídavné jméno: well **enough**.

items.en: The traffic was far too heavy this morning.
items.cz: Ten provoz byl dnes ráno až příliš hustý.
items.gap: The traffic was ____ too heavy this morning.
accepts: The traffic was far too heavy this morning.
The traffic was way too heavy this morning.
items.wrong: The traffic was very too heavy this morning.
items.explanation: To strengthen **too**, use **far** or **way**. *Very too* is impossible.
items.explanation_cz: Pro zesílení **too** se používá **far** nebo **way**. *Very too* nejde.
